brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Conceptually compelling spatial metaphor — clusters by topic instead of folders, with color-coded category labels anchoring zones
Per-document colored icon tiles give pleasant visual rhythm and quick recognition across the canvas
Toolbar is restrained and unobtrusive, letting the canvas itself be the primary affordance
dominant_weaknesses: Cards overlap and occlude text (Design System, Product, User Interviews) — the spatial layout actively destroys legibility
Category labels collide with cards and clip mid-word ('CORE ENGINEERING', 'USER RESEARCH'), suggesting no z-order or padding logic
Cluster boundaries are invisible — without hulls, tints, or connectors, proximity reads as accidental mess rather than semantic grouping
fix_priorities: Introduce collision avoidance and minimum spacing so no card overlaps another or its category label
Add subtle cluster shapes (tinted hulls or dashed regions) to make topic proximity legible at a glance
Establish a clear typographic hierarchy where category headers sit above the card layer with reserved space
Add faint connector lines or gravity wells between related docs to reinforce the 'spatial' narrative
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept is strong, but visceral polish is undermined and behavioral usability collapses under overlap and unclear grouping.
rationale.intent_fit: It gestures at the spatial-canvas brief but executes it poorly — proximity exists without legibility, so the metaphor reads as chaos rather than organization.
